metaDescription: Learn how to exit a TradingView trade in parts, adjusting quantity and setting multiple targets to lock in profits and manage risk gradually.
intro: Closing a position in parts, rather than all at once, lets you lock in profits gradually and manage risk more precisely. This guide covers using the TradingView order panel or broker integration to scale out of long or short positions on crypto, forex, or stocks.

steps.heading: Open the order panel or broker integration
steps.body: Access your position through TradingView's order panel or your connected broker to begin a partial close.

steps.heading: Adjust the quantity to close
steps.body: Specify how much of your position you want to exit, leaving the rest open for further movement.

steps.heading: Set multiple targets
steps.body: You can set several target levels so different portions of your position close at different price points.

steps.heading: Manage exits manually or with limit orders
steps.body: Choose whether to close portions manually as conditions change, or automate exits using limit orders.

steps.heading: Check paper trading limitations
steps.body: If you're using paper trading, be aware of current limitations around simulating partial exits, and look into possible workarounds.

steps.heading: Track your scaled exits
steps.body: Use TradingView's tools to keep a clear record of each partial exit as part of your overall trading plan.

faq.question: Can I close only part of a position on TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, you can adjust the quantity in the order panel or broker integration to exit a position in parts.

faq.question: Does partial closing work with paper trading?
faq.answer: Paper trading has some limitations for simulating partial exits, though workarounds exist depending on your setup.

faq.question: Can I set multiple profit targets for one trade?
faq.answer: Yes, you can set multiple targets so different portions of your position close at different price levels.

faq.question: Is partial closing useful for volatile markets?
faq.answer: Yes, it helps manage risk and lock in gains gradually, which is especially useful when trading volatile crypto or forex markets.

faq.question: Does this work for both long and short positions?
faq.answer: Yes, partial closing applies to both long and short positions depending on your trading strategy.
